questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of the first commercial robots
How robots are used in factories
Using robots to care for elderly and sick people
Why nurses are paid so little
questions.why: Rob says robots are being introduced in social care to look after the sick and elderly.

questions.q: What problem is mentioned about human carers?
options: There aren't enough of them for everyone who needs care
They don't get enough training to look after older people
They cost much more than robots over a whole year
They don't want to work alongside robots in care homes
questions.why: Sam says there are more people needing care than people who can help.

questions.q: What did the UK government announce?
options: A plan to train thousands more nurses
A £34 million fund to develop care robots
A ban on using robots in all care homes
Higher pay for care assistants from next year
questions.why: Sam mentions a £34 million fund to help develop robots to look after us.

questions.q: What can the robot Pepper NOT do?
options: Wave its hands
Turn around for privacy
Talk to people
Pick up or move things
questions.why: Abbey says it doesn't grip or move anything and can't provide physical assistance.

questions.q: What are the researchers mainly interested in testing with Pepper?
options: How well it works as someone to talk to
How quickly it can move around
Whether it can give medicine
How cheap it is to produce
questions.why: Abbey says they're more interested in how it works as a companion to talk and interact with.

questions.q: What is Sam's view about robots as companions?
options: Robots are better because they never get tired
Robots will soon understand people perfectly
A human would probably understand people better
Companions are not important for old people
questions.why: Sam says 'surely a human is better for that' because they understand you better.

questions.q: Why does Rob mention the 100,000 care assistant vacancies?
options: To show that care jobs are now very well paid
To argue that someone, or something, must do the work
To criticise the government for cutting care budgets
To encourage young listeners to apply for care jobs
questions.why: After the figure he asks, 'Who is going to do all the work?'

questions.q: What is Dr Sarah Woodin worried about?
options: Robots becoming too expensive for care homes to buy
Robots taking all the doctors' and nurses' jobs
Robots often breaking down in busy care homes
People being left with only robots to care for them
questions.why: She warns people 'might be housed and abandoned to robots' if robots replace people.
